thread:
elena: FYI noticed a token/sec regression on canary after today's runtime merge. Token/sec down ~12% on the 3pm canary runs, queue depth jumped and median batch size collapsed. cc @raj @sam

raj: Thanks — seeing the CI perf alert too. I started a quick profile; continuous-batcher has a big increase in wait time. Could be scheduler prefetch/pacing change in the merge.

sam: Can you paste the profiler/top sample output?

elena: Pprof snippet from the canary run:```
continuous_batcher_wait 42.1%
scheduler_prefetch_check 18.7%
kv_cache_lookup 9.8% (hit rate reported 72% vs baseline 78%)
kernel_select_path 8.4% (fallback path increased)
memcopy 6.3%
other 14.7%
```

perf-ci-bot: nightly-perf: regression detected (tokens/sec -11.9% vs baseline). Alert ID: perf-2145-ctb. Link: https://ci.internal/reports/perf-2145

raj: Bisect points to commit 7f9aab2 (runtime: adjust prefetch window and pacing heuristics). That commit changed prefetch_window default from 256->512 for startup, and switched to an eager prefetch check in scheduler. Looks like under our short-seq-heavy traffic that causes premature batch draining and smaller batches.

elena: Reproduced locally with trace enabled. If I set prefetch_window back to 128 on the canary config, queueing latency drops ~40% and tokens/sec recovers to -2% vs baseline. Also noticed kernel selection started choosing a fallback kernel for ~15% more short sequences after the commit (threshold tweak).

sam: Two quick mitigations: 1) hotfix canary config to prefetch_window=128 and revert the eager check; 2) open a rollback PR for the merge if rollout widespread. Which do you want first?

raj: I'll open a minimal rollback PR that reverts the scheduler pacing change (PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pull/3421) and a separate config change PR to set prefetch_window=128 for canary clusters (PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pull/3422). Deploy plan: apply the config change immediately to canary, monitor tokens/sec and kv_cache hit rate, then merge rollback once approvals in place.

elena: Also adding a perf regression test to perf-suite that sends a short-seq-heavy distribution (p50 seq=32, p90 seq=96, tokens per request low) and asserts tokens/sec within 5% of baseline. Will push test and a diagnostic metric: batch_size_p50 and continuous_batcher_idle_ms.

sam: Good. Also let's add a quick alert for kv_cache_hit drops >3% in 5m window — that flagged the kernel fallback problem early.

elena: On it. I'll patch canary now (prefetch_window=128) and post results in 10m. If we see recovery, we'll proceed with rollback PR review and hold rollout to prod until fix lands. :thumbsup:

raj: Thanks — tagging as rollout-blocker in the release board.

elena: Update: after prefetch_window change tokens/sec bounced to -1.8% and median batch size returned to expected. KV cache hit recovered to ~77%. I'll keep the canary under observation for 30m and then mark the incident resolved if stable.
